Brick.label: Brick Hardcastle (Leading Man)
Brick.description: Deep, resonant male baritone, 1940s Hollywood matinee idol, over-enunciated and self-important, slight Western drawl, confident and vain.
Brick.sample: Stand back, little lady. Hardcastle is on the scene, and the camera simply adores this jawline. Never fear! I do all of my own stunts, and most of my own dialogue. Now, which way is my good side?

Vivienne.label: Dame Vivienne Sterling (Diva)
Vivienne.description: Older female, Mid-Atlantic accent, grand theatrical stage actress, imperious and dramatic, crisp diction, capable of operatic shrieks.
Vivienne.sample: Darling, I have been acting since before you were a rumor. This is my scene, my light, and my monologue. Is no one watching the set? How dare you, gravity! Someone fetch my lawyer, and a very large pillow.

Gus.label: Gus Pickles (Nervous PA)
Gus.description: Young male, fast and high-pitched, nervous and eager, frequent voice cracks, breathy, apologetic.
Gus.sample: Uh, quiet on set! Please? Thanks! Sorry! Is that supposed to be wobbling? Oh no, oh no, oh no. I got it, I got it! Don't worry, I'll just fix this, and, oh no. Am I fired? I feel like I'm fired.

Director.label: The Director (the player)
Director.description: Middle-aged male film director shouting through a megaphone, passionate and theatrical.
Director.sample: Quiet on set! Places, everyone! Roll camera, and aaand, action! Cut! Cut! Beautiful. Print it! Again, from the top! Let's make cinema history, people, one disaster at a time.

FirstAD.label: First Assistant Director
FirstAD.description: Female, dry, deadpan, efficient stage manager, talks over a radio.
FirstAD.sample: Call sheet's up, boss. Actors to set, please. We're losing the light. Fire marshal's on his way. Insurance called, again. That was the two-million-dollar camera. Scene one, take thirty-seven.
